facts.statement: The holotype fossil was discovered in February 2001 during an expedition in the Sierra Barrosa locality, 30 km north-east of Plaza Huincul in Neuquén province.
facts.quote: In February 2001 the Museo Carmen Funes conducted a joint expedition with the Royal Tyrell Museum at the Sierra Barrosa Locality, 30 km north-east of Plaza Huincul, Neuquén province.

facts.statement: The genus name Barrosasuchus combines the locality name Sierra Barrosa with a Greek word meaning crocodile.
facts.quote: The generic name derives from the Sierra Barrosa locality where the fossils have been found and the , () meaning crocodile.

facts.statement: The species name neuquenianus refers to the Neuquén Province where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: The species epithet refers to the Neuquén Province.

facts.statement: The genus Barrosasuchus contains only one known species, Barrosasuchus neuquenianus.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Barrosasuchus neuquenianus.

facts.statement: It is estimated that Barrosasuchus had up to 13 maxillary teeth on each side of the skull, plus 4 teeth on each premaxilla.
facts.quote: It is estimated that Barrosasuchus may have had up to 13 maxillary teeth (10 of which were preserved) on each side of the skull in addition to 4 teeth on each premaxilla.

facts.statement: A conspicuous foramen at the midpoint of the symphysial suture serves an unknown purpose but is considered an autapomorphy of Barrosasuchus.
facts.quote: Dorsally the symphysial suture has a conspicuous foramen at its mid-point that serves an unknown purpose, but serves as one of Barrosasuchus autapomorphies.

facts.statement: Three types of osteoderms—rectangular, square, and round—are preserved, with most scattered on the ventral side, though a small section of the posterior preserves articulate ventral armor.
facts.quote: 3 types of osteoderms are preserved, rectangular, square and round, most of which are no longer articulated and scattered over the ventral side of the holotype, obscuring other elements of the fossil, however a small section of the posterior still preserves articulate ventral armor.

facts.statement: Square and rounded osteoderms contacted each other to form the ventral shield.
facts.quote: The square and rounded osteoderms contacted each other and would have formed the ventral shield.

facts.statement: Barrosasuchus lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Argentina, specifically in Patagonia.
facts.quote: Barrosasuchus is a genus of peirosaurid notosuchian from the Santonian of Argentina and part of the extensive peirosaurid record of Late Cretaceous Patagonia.

facts.statement: Barrosasuchus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Barrosasuchus is classified as a peirosaurid notosuchian.
facts.quote: Barrosasuchus is a genus of peirosaurid notosuchian from the Santonian of Argentina and part of the extensive peirosaurid record of Late Cretaceous Patagonia.

facts.statement: The parent group of Barrosasuchus is the family Peirosauridae.
Barrosasuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
The genus Barrosasuchus was described by Coria et al. in 2018.
The type species of the genus Barrosasuchus is Barrosasuchus neuquenianus.
